results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

output_document.summary: Last quarter's incident occurred when the API rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute without the required 24-hour advance notice, causing multiple clients to experience 2-4 hour outages. The postmortem identified three key lessons for the new webhooks feature: (1) all limit changes must include a mandatory 72-hour advance notice period, (2) clients need a clearly documented escalation path for support, and (3) rate limit headers should be consistently included in all API responses to provide transparency. These requirements should be built into the webhooks feature design from the start to prevent similar communication failures.
